rationale: Three lenses ran on the backend half (blind, edge-case with repo access, acceptance against spec). All three converged on a critical wire-contract defect (CR-001) and on the loss of server-side answer validation (CR-003). The edge-case lens verified several findings empirically against the real validator/converter rather than by reading code. CR-001 was fixed inline during the review (commit 'Fix capability field wire alias') and is recorded here as resolved-during-review for the audit trail. One blind/edge-case finding (customer-config test banner) was DISMISSED after verification: the file is an uncommitted local working-tree edit that is not part of the branch; it appeared only because the reviewed diff was initially built with 'git diff BASE' instead of 'BASE..HEAD' — the diff was rebuilt correctly. Deferred (not emitted as findings, recorded here): wire-level names leak outside the adapter module (v1.0-readiness weaker than spec §2.1 claims, adapter.wrap_chunk is dead code); the BE<->FE contract freshness test skips in backend CI rather than failing; the tool raises a generic ValueError instead of the SDK's VALIDATION_FAILED shape; convert_history failure logs omit the conversation id. Frontend half is reviewed separately. Coverage note: the backend diff is ~5.7k lines — large but reviewed in full by all three lenses.

findings.problem: a2ui_supported_catalogs had no explicit alias, so its wire name was a2UiSupportedCatalogs while the frontend sends a2uiSupportedCatalogs; the value was silently dropped and the capability gate could never open.
findings.impact: Feature dead end-to-end in production while all backend tests stayed green (tests built the model by python field name).
findings.recommendation: Add alias plus wire-level regression tests including an end-to-end gate test built from the frontend payload.
findings.status: RESOLVED during review (commit 'EPMCDME-13912: Fix capability field wire alias')

findings.problem: The agent-authored surface lost the removed breadth/size bounds (legacy enforced MAX_SURFACE_ELEMENTS=100 and MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES=65536); only SDK nesting-depth validation remains.
findings.impact: Measured: 3000 Text components (775 KB) validate clean in 2.85 s, are streamed, persisted into conversations.history and re-serialized into the prompt on every later turn — permanent token/storage bloat from one steered tool call.
findings.recommendation: Cap len(components) and the serialized size of components+data_model in execute() before building envelopes; raise ValueError so the model can retry with a smaller surface.

findings.problem: No semantic validation of the submitted data model or action name against the stored surface: option membership, selection caps, length caps, date bounds, regex checks and unknown data-model keys are all unchecked, and action.name is never matched to a Button in the surface. validate_a2ui_intake returns the stored surface envelopes but the caller discards them.
findings.impact: Spec §2.6 requires the ported anti-tampering checks. As shipped, a client can submit values and action names the surface never offered, and up to 64 KB of attacker-chosen text is replayed into the LLM prompt under a trusted '[Structured response to surface ...]' framing.
findings.recommendation: Consume the returned surface envelopes, index components by id, and re-validate the data model against them (allowed keys, option subset, selection cap, string length, date bounds, validationRegexp) plus action.name against Button event names; add a test per check.

findings.problem: _validate_a2ui_action returns immediately when a2ui_action is None, but conversation_service persists a2ui_data_model unconditionally.
findings.impact: A request carrying a2uiDataModel without a2uiAction bypasses ownership re-check, surface existence, already-answered and the 64 KB cap; a multi-MB blob is written into conversation history and re-serialized on every conversation GET.
findings.recommendation: Validate when either field is present, and reject (or drop) a data model submitted without a matching action.

findings.problem: Synthesized component ids (root, <button>-label, <parent>-c<i>) can collide with agent-authored legacy ids, and convert_history never validates its own output — a message only counts as failed when conversion raises.
findings.impact: Verified against the real validator: legacy surfaces with an element id 'root', or an id colliding with '<btn>-label', produce 'Duplicate component ID' envelopes that are written to the database and logged as successfully converted; the renderer cannot render them and reverse_request returns an empty surface for those rows.
findings.recommendation: Validate converted envelopes inside convert_message/convert_history and count validation errors as failed (leave the message untouched, log the conversation id); de-collide synthesized ids against existing ones.

findings.problem: Rolling back the release destroys the assistant toggle: d1c2 downgrade re-adds interactive_features as empty JSONB, then e7f8 downgrade drops interactive_enabled with no reverse backfill.
findings.impact: After a rollback every assistant that had interactive features enabled reads as disabled, with no recovery short of a DB restore.
findings.recommendation: Make d1c2 downgrade reconstruct the JSONB from interactive_enabled before the boolean is dropped (or defer the drop to a later release).

findings.problem: GeneratedMessage no longer declares the legacy fields and the whole history list is re-dumped on every update, so the first new turn in a legacy conversation silently erases interactive_request/interactive_response.
findings.impact: The migration's downgrade predicate requires those legacy fields, so downgrade becomes a no-op for any conversation touched after deploy; worse, a conversation continued before the migration job runs loses its interactive history in both protocols.
findings.recommendation: Keep the legacy fields on GeneratedMessage as deprecated pass-through until the downgrade window closes, or document the migration as one-way and gate the deploy so it completes before chat traffic is served.
